_meta.description: What Amazon last said about each listing, from the ListingsItems API: main image, status, identity (FNSKU, product type, created and last-updated dates), variation role and issues. One row per (store_id, country_code, seller_sku), refreshed in place after each GET_MERCHANT_LISTINGS_ALL_DATA sync: new SKUs first, then every listing the seller changed since the last sync, and a rolling re-read that reaches every listing within 30 days (Amazon's own changes, such as a suppression, do not move lastUpdatedDate). Group children under parent_sku to build families; variation_role says which row is the parent. No date in the unique key, so report_date='latest' applies no date filter here (omitting it works too) — never pin an explicit date, which would return only the SKUs touched by the newest enrichment batch.

columns.note: FK to amazon_stores.store_id
Marketplace country code e.g. AE, SA, US
Merchant SKU
ASIN from ListingsItems API (nullable)
Main product image URL from Amazon CDN (nullable if no image or enrichment failed)
Listing status string from ListingsItems API e.g. BUYABLE (nullable)
Timestamp when this row was last fetched/inserted
Variation parent's seller SKU for a child listing; the listing's own SKU for a parent; NULL for a standalone listing (from the ListingsItems relationships)
The variation parent's ASIN when known (a parent's own; a child's once its parent's row is cached); NULL otherwise
When Amazon last answered this SKU's variation relationships; NULL = not asked yet (filled on a later enrichment pass)

Amazon's variation role for this SKU: parent, child or standalone, from the listing's own relationships; NULL = not read yet (then fall back to parent_sku). A listing with no variation relationship is standalone even when its ASIN is a variation child in the catalog.
Amazon's fulfillment network SKU (summaries fnSku); NULL for a variation parent or a listing without one
Amazon product type of the listing, e.g. EXERCISE_MAT

Amazon's createdDate for the listing. UTC instant (timestamptz). Query results show it in the store ref's marketplace local time, without an offset; a bare date in a filter is that marketplace's midnight.

Amazon's lastUpdatedDate for the listing — it moves on the seller's own edits only, not when Amazon changes the listing. UTC instant (timestamptz). Query results show it in the store ref's marketplace local time, without an offset.
The worst issue Amazon reports on the listing: ERROR, WARNING, or NONE (no issues, or informational ones only); NULL = not checked yet
Every enforcement action on the listing's issues, sorted and comma-separated, e.g. LISTING_SUPPRESSED,SEARCH_SUPPRESSED; NULL when there is none
Up to 10 issues, worst first: [{code, severity, message (at most 500 characters), attributeNames, enforcements}]; [] = none; NULL = not checked yet
When Amazon's issues for this listing were last read; NULL = never. UTC instant (timestamptz). Query results show it in the store ref's marketplace local time, without an offset.

Why the row was last read: new, retry, backfill (a column it lacked), delta (the seller changed the listing), sweep (the rolling re-read), refresh (a person asked for it), reread (an issue or brand-content change)

When the last listing status or issue change Amazon notified for this listing happened; status and issue_* are as of this time when it is later than the last read. NULL = none received. UTC instant (timestamptz).
The kind of that notification: LISTINGS_ITEM_STATUS_CHANGE or LISTINGS_ITEM_ISSUES_CHANGE
